chunk-001:c002.proposition: Inconceivability is an unreliable guide to metaphysical necessity because intuitions depend on revisable conceptual schemes and apparently inconceivable alternatives can become intelligible.

orphanFallback.rationale: Independently of any retained opposing move, the examples of revisable conceptual schemes positively establish epistemic caution about inferring metaphysical necessity from conceivability.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Possible-world quantification alone does not distinguish logical, epistemic, and metaphysical necessity, because each modality depends on how the relevant worlds or models are restricted.

orphanFallback.rationale: As a constructive distinction among modalities, the move shows that truth across possible worlds requires an independently specified restriction before it identifies metaphysical necessity.

chunk-001:c010.proposition: Propositions may possess intentionality without being mental, so the inference from their directedness to their status as thoughts requires independent defense.

orphanFallback.rationale: The proposition independently advances a nonmental account of propositional aboutness and identifies the additional premise needed to infer mentality from intentionality.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: Frege's communication argument supports objective, shareable propositional contents, while treating such contents as divine thoughts merely redescribes the required third ontological category.

orphanFallback.rationale: The communication argument independently supports objective and shareable contents distinct from individual human thoughts, supplying a positive basis for proposition realism.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: If a divine thought is identical with its own propositional content, its aboutness generates an ungrounded self-referential regress rather than determinate content.

orphanFallback.rationale: Considered constructively, the regress exposes a coherence requirement for any divine-thought theory: its proposed content must ground out in something determinate rather than itself alone.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: Treating divine thoughts as propositional contents without contents of their own abandons the familiar intentional character used to motivate their classification as thoughts.

orphanFallback.rationale: The move independently establishes an internal constraint on divine conceptualism: its ultimate contents must retain the intentional features that initially motivated the appeal to thoughts.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: Divine thoughts resemble intrinsically intentional abstract propositions so closely that calling them mental provides no clear explanatory benefit over Platonism.

orphanFallback.rationale: As a standalone comparison, the move presents Platonism as retaining intrinsically intentional propositions and requires a distinct explanatory gain before adding divine mentality.

chunk-003:c003-02.proposition: A Platonist can reverse the proposed explanation by treating propositions as the source from which ordinary thoughts derive their intentionality.

orphanFallback.rationale: The reversed grounding proposal constructively supplies a nonmental explanation of aboutness: thoughts become intentional through propositions occurring as their contents.

chunk-003:c003-05.proposition: A paradox that afflicts both divine conceptualism and Platonist realism cannot discriminate between them and therefore supplies no comparative support for either account.

orphanFallback.rationale: The proposition independently establishes a comparative standard: liabilities shared by both realist theories are neutral and cannot ground an explanatory advantage.

chunk-003:c003-06.proposition: Mathematical discovery, imperfect physical representations, and communication support realism about propositions or abstract objects independently of divine conceptualism.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source offers this as a positive realist case: discovered truths appear independent of their imperfect physical representations and of human construction.
